findings.title: rubric-audit.js and attack-design.js are never invoked by any CLI verb
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:528, :958, :1068 — launch lines exist for verify-architecture.js/severity-recheck.js/dismissals.js, none for these two
findings.description: Of the eleven workflow scripts, nine are wired into a gbg verb that builds their args and prints their launch line (every "*.js" literal in src/ and ext/ is only: audit.js, dismissals.js, hunt.js, lanes.js, panel.js, severity-recheck.js, verify-act.js, verify-architecture.js, verify-state.js). rubric-audit.js and attack-design.js never appear anywhere in src/ or ext/. Neither script's args/output shape is documented in its instrument's schema.json, and no schema/*.json exists for either output, unlike every other script. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md documents both as delivered v1.0.0 contributions (D17, §6.8: "attack-design.js ... is the instrument every lens list must survive"), but no gbg command can actually launch either.
findings.resolution_hint: Add a CLI verb (or fold into an existing one) that constructs args for rubric-audit.js and attack-design.js and prints their launch line, plus matching schema entries.

findings.title: dismissals.js and verify-architecture.js never instruct the agent to echo the finding id
locations: instruments/bug-hunt/workflow/dismissals.js:19-28 (SCHEMA `id: { type: 'string' }`, no description) and :31-51 (prompt never says "return id=...")
instruments/check-consistency/workflow/verify-act.js:35 — `id: { type: 'string', description: 'the finding id EXACTLY as given' }` (contrast)
findings.description: dismissals.js and verify-architecture.js ask one agent per finding to return {id, verdict, evidence,...} but never tell it what to put in id — no schema description, no explicit "return id=" instruction — unlike severity-recheck.js and verify-act.js which do this explicitly. schema/dismissal.schema.json and schema/architecture-fix.schema.json both require id to match a strict `round/lane#n` pattern, and each script's own liveness check (`A.items.filter(i => !verdicts.some(v => v.id === i.id))`) silently reclassifies a correctly-audited finding as "auditor DIED" if the model paraphrases the id.
findings.resolution_hint: Add description: 'the finding id EXACTLY as given' to the id property, and an explicit Return {id: "${f.id}", ...} line, matching severity-recheck.js/verify-act.js.

findings.title: severity-recheck.js and attack-design.js write A.round without validating it was supplied
findings.description: Both scripts document 'round' as part of Args and write it into their output, but neither's required-arg guard (`for (const k of [...]) if (A[k]===undefined) throw`) includes 'round', unlike every sibling script that writes round (lanes.js, panel.js, audit.js, hunt.js, dismissals.js all validate it). If round were omitted, JSON.stringify silently drops the undefined property instead of throwing the clear 'args.round is required' error every other script gives.
findings.resolution_hint: Add 'round' to the required-arg check list in both scripts.

findings.title: hunt.js's free-lane prompt references invariants that were never named
locations: instruments/bug-hunt/workflow/hunt.js:94 — `(the one file under .gbg/ you may open besides the invariants named above)`
instruments/bug-hunt/workflow/hunt.js:68-76 (FREE_PREAMBLE, used for this branch, never mentions invariants)
instruments/bug-hunt/workflow/hunt.js:85 — the invariants line lives only in HUNT_PREAMBLE, the other branch
findings.description: For a kind==='free' lane, the prompt is FREE_PREAMBLE + "WHERE TO START: ... (the one file under .gbg/ you may open besides the invariants named above)". But FREE_PREAMBLE never names any invariants file — only HUNT_PREAMBLE (the other branch) conditionally adds the invariants line when A.invariants_path is set. The free-lane agent is told invariants were 'named above' when nothing was ever named in its own prompt — a dangling reference copied from the territory-lane phrasing.
findings.resolution_hint: Either add the invariants line to FREE_PREAMBLE too, or drop 'besides the invariants named above' from the free-lane suffix.

findings.title: attack-design.js's header comment documents an args field the code never reads
locations: instruments/audit-changes/workflow/attack-design.js:5 — `// Args: { ..., subject: {object, defect, defects, lanes, context, directions, standpoint, source}, ... }`
instruments/audit-changes/workflow/attack-design.js:16-19 — only object, defects (plural), context, standpoint, source are read
findings.description: The header comment lists subject.defect (singular) as an args field, but the code only ever reads S.defects (plural); subject.defect is never referenced anywhere in the file.
findings.resolution_hint: Drop 'defect' from the header comment's args listing.
